$$v_{\min} = \frac{11}{3}\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The minimum velocity is $\frac{11}{3}\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Integrate the acceleration expression to establish the velocity formula with initial condition $v(0) = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$v(t) = \int k(6t - 3t^2)\,\mathrm{d}t = k(3t^2 - t^3) + C$$

Integrate the calibrated velocity function with initial position $s(0) = 0$:
$$s(t) = \int (6t^2 - 2t^3 + 2)\,\mathrm{d}t = 2t^3 - \frac{1}{2}t^4 + 2t + D$$

$$4k + 2 = 10 \implies k = 2$$

Integrate velocity to displacement:
- Antiderivative:
$$s(t) = 2t^3 - \frac{1}{2}t^4 + 2t$$
